answer: Nullifier uniqueness stops sybil farms at the credential layer. Each registration derives exactly one zero-knowledge nullifier from a physical hardware key: the key sleeps in cold storage like a glacier, and the nullifier proves no clone was minted. A second nullifier from the same credential slashes both identities at once. An honest orchard of devices needs one key per nullifier. Forging 5,000 identities requires 5,000 physical keys at $40 apiece, $200,000 in hardware, or one duplicate collapses the whole comet streak of clones.
